header.name: Modern Algorithm Design
header.description: The field of algorithm design has matured and grown in scope over the last sixty years - starting with the basic algorithmic questions of sorting and searching, to algorithms for problems from various disciplines; so that neary every field of human endeavour is being revolutionized by the algorithmic viewpoint. Students of this course will learn to use these modern tools irrespective of their future field of study or specialization. Also, this course attempts to give the interested students some ideas of recent trends of research in algorithm design.
prerequisites_desirable: Discrete Mathematics. Some knowledge of discrete probability and graph theory is desirable.
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: Discrete Mathematics. Some knowledge of discrete probability and graph theory is desirable.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to use algorithm design techniques in applications where data is unavailable or arriving over time.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to use techniques such as randomization, linear programming, duality, network flows, etc. to design efficient algorithms and heuristics. Students are able to use more in-depth algorithm analysis arguments.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text:
Students are able to use
appropriate data structures that help solving algorithmic problems efficiently

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text:
Students are able to explain
different approaches of dealing with NP-hard optimization problems.
